note: Curated classroom lesson seeds for steady, inspectable simulation runs, now with local animation picks and author-defined custom games.

lessons.title: Medieval Bavaria: duchies, monasteries, and the Wittelsbach rise
lessons.subject: history
lessons.essential_question: How did political power, monastic culture, and imperial ties shape medieval Bavaria?
objectives: Explain how the stem duchy of Bavaria fit into the Holy Roman Empire.
Trace the political significance of the Ottonians, Welfs, and Wittelsbachs.
Connect monastic reform and trade routes to regional power.
lessons.source_excerpt: Classroom excerpt adapted from medieval Bavarian chronicle themes: regional order rested on a fragile braid of ducal loyalty, episcopal influence, monastic reform, and routes that moved salt, silver, texts, and pilgrims through the Alpine edge.
lessons.source_attribution: Synthetic teaching excerpt based on chronicler motifs from Ottonian and twelfth-century Bavaria.
teaching_notes: Begin with a slow map-reading warmup so students place Bavaria within the Holy Roman Empire before naming dynasties.
Pause after the Investiture Conflict to distinguish imperial authority from local ducal power.
Close by asking how monasteries and trade routes stabilized both culture and political memory.

phases.title: Orient the map
phases.purpose: Locate Bavaria in relation to imperial power and neighboring routes.
phases.facilitator_move: Project a map and ask students to notice what routes and borders imply before naming rulers.
phases.learner_signal: Students describe position, movement, and exposure rather than reciting facts.

phases.title: Trace conflict and dynasty
phases.purpose: Connect imperial tension to local political change.
phases.facilitator_move: Slowly compare the Ottonians, Welfs, and Wittelsbachs through a cause-and-effect discussion.
phases.learner_signal: Students explain why a conflict could reshape who governed Bavaria.

phases.title: Synthesize institutions
phases.purpose: Blend monastic, political, and commercial forces into one interpretation.
phases.facilitator_move: Ask for a written explanation that links abbeys, roads, and ducal legitimacy.
phases.learner_signal: Students move from isolated details to a coherent system view.

concept_threads.label: Imperial belonging
concept_threads.question: How did Bavaria belong to something larger than itself?
concept_threads.significance: This thread anchors the duchy inside the Holy Roman Empire rather than treating it as isolated.

concept_threads.label: Institutional memory
concept_threads.question: Why did monasteries matter beyond religion?
concept_threads.significance: Monasteries stabilized literacy, landholding, and elite networks.

concept_threads.label: Routes and rule
concept_threads.question: How did movement of people and goods reinforce authority?
concept_threads.significance: Trade and travel made power visible, taxable, and repeatable.

discussion_prompts: Why might monasteries matter politically as well as spiritually in medieval Bavaria?
How did imperial struggles change the power of Bavarian rulers?
What does trade reveal about the relationship between geography and authority?
lessons.response_prompt: In 3 to 5 sentences, explain how ducal power, monastic institutions, and imperial politics interacted in medieval Bavaria.

response_rubric.label: Claim Clarity
response_rubric.guidance: Open with a precise historical claim.

response_rubric.label: Evidence Use
response_rubric.guidance: Name institutions, dynasties, or terms from the lesson.

response_rubric.label: Causal Reasoning
response_rubric.guidance: Explain how conflict, religion, and commerce shaped one another.

response_rubric.label: Calm Framing
response_rubric.guidance: Keep the explanation measured and coherent.

response_rubric.label: Inquiry Posture
response_rubric.guidance: Show reflective synthesis rather than listing.

activities.title: Quiet Timeline
activities.description: Place the major phases into a chronological arc before interpreting them.
activities.prompt: Place these historical phases into a steady chronological flow.
activities.success_message: The timeline settles into order. The political arc is becoming clearer.

activities.title: Power Checkpoint
activities.description: Test whether the learner can identify the institutional hinge in the lesson.
activities.prompt: Which institution most directly preserved literacy, landholding, and elite memory in medieval Bavaria?
activities.explanation: Monasteries shaped literacy, record-keeping, land management, and elite networks.
activities.success_message: The institutional layer comes into focus.

activities.title: Source Evidence Weave
activities.description: Select the excerpt details that most directly support the lesson's central explanation of power.
activities.prompt: Choose the cards that directly support the claim that imperial ties, monasteries, and trade shaped medieval Bavaria.
activities.explanation: The strongest evidence cards show imperial structure, monastic institutions, and routes of movement working together rather than in isolation.
activities.success_message: The evidence weave holds. The lesson now reads as a system rather than a list.

items.label: Ducal loyalty tied Bavaria to the Holy Roman Empire.
Monastic reform helped preserve literacy, landholding, and political memory.
Trade routes moved goods, texts, and pilgrims through the region.
Baltic shipyards governed Bavarian mountain villages directly.
Harvest festivals alone determined ducal succession.

activities.title: Forest Charter Parade
activities.description: A lesson-authored sequencing game where the seminar mascots carry the institutional story one link at a time.
activities.prompt: Guide the teddy scribe and the young deer route-guide through the order that turns regional memory into stable rule.
activities.success_message: The parade settles into order. Institution, route, and ducal authority now read as one civic chain.

config.support_text: Start with the memory-keeping institution, then move outward toward circulation and recognized authority.
config.completion_message: The custom game confirms that monasteries, routes, and ducal legitimacy formed a linked system.

tokens.label: Ducal Legitimacy
tokens.hint: Turns stable networks into visible rule.

lessons.title: Medieval Bavaria: towns, salt, and Alpine routes
lessons.subject: history
lessons.essential_question: How did commerce and geography shape daily life and authority in medieval Bavaria?
objectives: Describe how salt and river trade affected Bavarian towns.
Explain why Alpine and Danube routes mattered to political power.
Compare urban growth with monastic and ducal influence.
lessons.source_excerpt: A teaching fragment for seminar use: towns grew where goods could pause, be taxed, protected, and rerouted; power followed not only castles and abbeys but roads, ferries, pack trains, and river docks.
lessons.source_attribution: Synthetic teaching excerpt inspired by medieval Bavarian trade geography.
teaching_notes: Use a quiet compare-and-contrast activity between monastery, market town, and ducal seat.
Have students trace one good, such as salt, from extraction to market to taxation.
Invite students to discuss how geography quietly structures power before naming specific rulers.

phases.title: Follow a good
phases.purpose: Turn commerce into a human-scale story of movement and control.
phases.facilitator_move: Ask students to narrate one shipment of salt across a route.
phases.learner_signal: Students see trade as a chain of places, permissions, and risks.

phases.title: Name the chokepoints
phases.facilitator_move: Pause over ferries, river crossings, and passes as leverage points.
phases.learner_signal: Students infer why routes could matter as much as city walls.

phases.title: Compare civic forms
phases.purpose: Distinguish market, monastic, and ducal centers.
phases.facilitator_move: Run a sorting or matching exercise before discussion.
phases.learner_signal: Students compare institutions by function instead of appearance.

concept_threads.label: Mobility
concept_threads.question: What moves through Bavaria, and who gains from that movement?
concept_threads.significance: Trade routes organize both wealth and hierarchy.

concept_threads.label: Civic permission
concept_threads.question: Why do charters and tolls matter?
concept_threads.significance: Authority depends on the right to regulate exchange.

concept_threads.label: Geographic leverage
concept_threads.question: How does terrain quietly shape political power?
concept_threads.significance: Rivers, passes, and crossings act as hidden political engines.

discussion_prompts: Why would controlling a route matter as much as controlling a city?
How did economic life reinforce political hierarchy?
What makes a market town different from a religious center?
lessons.response_prompt: Explain how trade routes and town growth helped organize power in medieval Bavaria.

response_rubric.label: Claim Clarity
response_rubric.guidance: State how geography and commerce shaped authority.

response_rubric.label: Evidence Use
response_rubric.guidance: Use concrete route, town, or toll details.

response_rubric.label: Causal Reasoning
response_rubric.guidance: Explain how movement and control reinforced one another.

response_rubric.label: Calm Framing
response_rubric.guidance: Keep the response ordered and measured.

response_rubric.label: Inquiry Posture
response_rubric.guidance: Compare institutions rather than merely naming them.

activities.title: Route and Role
activities.description: Match civic elements to the function they performed inside the trade network.
activities.prompt: Match each civic element to its historical function.
activities.success_message: The network aligns. Trade, rule, and daily life sit in relation.

activities.title: Route Reasoning
activities.description: Check whether the learner recognizes why chokepoints matter.
activities.prompt: Why could a river crossing become politically important in medieval Bavaria?
choices: It let rulers tax, protect, and regulate movement
It removed the need for markets
It prevented monasteries from owning land
activities.explanation: Control of crossings made transport predictable, taxable, and politically valuable.
activities.success_message: The geographic logic of authority is now visible.

activities.title: Trade Evidence Weave
activities.description: Choose the evidence cards that best support the lesson's claim about routes and authority.
activities.prompt: Select the details that most directly show how trade routes and geography organized power in medieval Bavaria.
activities.explanation: The best evidence names movement, chokepoints, and formal permission because those made commerce politically useful.
activities.success_message: The route logic settles into place. Geography and authority now reinforce one another.

items.label: Crossings and ferries allowed rulers to tax and regulate movement.
Market charters made exchange predictable and authorized.
Salt roads and river routes linked towns into repeatable networks of power.
Trade eliminated the need for any local authority.
One monastery personally controlled every Bavarian route at once.

activities.title: Market Lantern Weave
activities.description: A custom lesson game that asks learners to build the route logic of political power from authored clue cards.
activities.prompt: Set the lantern cards into the order that best explains how movement became authority.
activities.success_message: The lantern path is complete. Trade, charter, and toll logic now reinforce one another.

config.support_text: Think in terms of movement first, then permission, then the revenue and leverage that follow.
config.completion_message: This custom path shows how roads and river crossings became repeatable engines of civic power.
